script.source:
//@version=5
indicator("uct-rsi-atr-parity-v1", overlay=false)
rsi14 = ta.rsi(close, 14)
atr14 = ta.atr(14)
plot(rsi14, title="rsi14")
plot(atr14, title="atr14")

provenance.note: Captured via CSV export (Table view -> Download data) of a real SPY Daily chart with a live ta.rsi(close,14)/ta.atr(14) indicator added, full double-precision floats. 1,328 real trading-day bars (2021-05-24 .. 2026-09-04), ALL rows carry a real vendor value. This window is a 5.3-year trailing slice of SPY's real, decades-long chart history -- the real vendor ta.atr(14) value at every one of these bars is already fully steady-state/converged (SPY's true first bar was in 1993), while UCT's own atr(...) computed over ONLY this captured window necessarily re-seeds cold at this window's own first bar. Measured: this cold-start effect (up to ~25% relative delta at bar 14) is 1-2 orders of magnitude LARGER than and confounds the already-adjudicated bar-0/TR-definition seed difference (divergences.json::atr-tr-starts-at-bar-1, measured there at ~0.23% at the seed via a spec-derived estimate over a continuous real-history run) -- this capture cannot cleanly isolate that smaller effect from the larger window-truncation artifact, and does not attempt to re-adjudicate it. What IS confirmed, for the first time with REAL vendor data: once past the capture-window's own convergence tail, UCT and the real vendor agree on ATR to float precision (~1e-9 relative) on REAL, CURRENT market data -- directly corroborating the ruling's own 'the delta is invisible where it is read' conclusion, not reopening it. This capture also cannot re-test the ruling's separate ALIGNMENT claim (one fewer emitted value at a symbol's true first-ever bar), since this window starts decades after SPY's real inception -- disclosed as out of this capture's reach, not silently assumed confirmed.

_vendor_parity_warmup_bars_note: Same capture-methodology rationale as the RSI observation's note -- 180 is a conservative round number past the empirically observed convergence point (last disagreeing index measured at 169 of 1328), not the semantic 14-bar period-warmup.
